question: In C++, which access specifier makes the inherited public and protected members of the base class protected in the derived class?

question: Which mechanism enables runtime (dynamic) polymorphism in C++?
option_b: Virtual functions called through base-class pointers/references
explanation: virtual functions + base pointer/reference produce dynamic dispatch. Overloading, operator overloading and templates resolve at compile time (static polymorphism).

question: Why should a base class destructor be declared virtual?
option_a: So derived destructors run when deleting a derived object through a base pointer
explanation: A virtual destructor ensures the derived class destructor is invoked during delete through a base-class pointer, avoiding resource leaks and undefined behaviour.

question: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) means:
option_a: Resources like memory/files are acquired in a constructor and released in the matching destructor
option_b: Resources are freed by the garbage collector
option_d: Resources are acquired on demand by the OS only
explanation: RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime: acquire in constructor, release in destructor, so exceptions and scope exit clean up automatically (smart pointers).
